scenes.chapter: Prologue — The Man in the Sunglasses

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (It's the diner. Same booths, same cracked vinyl, same smell of burnt coffee. Except it's raining. Inside.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Water coming down through the ceiling in slow sheets and nothing's getting wet.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (No Linda. No Brandon. Every booth full of nobody.)
You always sit facing the door.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (There's a man in my booth. My booth. Black jacket. Sunglasses, indoors, in the dark.)
Not because you're brave. Because you want the extra two seconds.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Do I know you?
No.
That's going to be the funniest part later, but sure. No.
The glasses stay on. There's nothing behind the left one and you'd be polite about it, which I'd hate.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He's wearing a sport watch. Left wrist. Same as mine.)
Let me ask you something and I want the honest answer, not the one you'd give Linda.
One year. Three hundred and sixty-five days of being pleasant. Of saying it's fine, of saying no worries, of letting things slide off you like you're built for it.
Name one thing it bought you.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I've got an answer. It's Riley. It's Mason. It's Pete keeping a seat for me without being asked.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I don't say it. And he waits exactly as long as it would take me to say it, and then he nods like I did.)
Okay.
Hold onto that one. You'll want it later, and I want to be there when it stops working.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The rain gets louder. He's still sitting there when the diner goes.)
Go on. Alarm's been going eleven minutes.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Four hours. The ceiling has a water stain shaped like an island. Some mornings it's Java. Some mornings it's nothing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (There was a dream. There's always a dream. This one had a face in it and I already can't hold onto it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (One year today. Nobody's going to say it. That's fine. That's the deal.)

exploration.prompt: Room 214. Fourteen minutes before hall check.

interactables.label: The camera on the desk
interactables.internal_thought: (Second-hand. Bought with three months of the allowance Mama sends. She thinks I bought textbooks. I did buy textbooks. Just not with that.)

interactables.label: Prayer mat, folded on the chair
interactables.internal_thought: (Fajr was at 5:52. I was awake at 5:40 and I let it go past. I don't know what that means yet. I keep not deciding.)

interactables.label: Photograph taped inside the wardrobe door
interactables.internal_thought: (Purwokerto. The kitchen. Mama, Bapak, me at eleven with a haircut I'd like to formally apologise for.)
interactables.follow_up: (I keep it inside the door so it's mine and not a conversation.)

interactables.label: Laptop, still open, still warm
interactables.internal_thought: (Forty-one tabs. Timeline for Maddie's edit, a half-finished script that does nothing, and a documentary about the 2013 storm I've started six times and never finished.)
interactables.follow_up: (I always stop it at the same place. The part where they list the names.)

interactables.label: Headphones
interactables.internal_thought: (Aura. Same playlist. Same song at the top of it. Four hundred and some plays of one Strokes track because it's the only thing that makes the noise in my head line up straight.)

interactables.label: Sport watch
interactables.internal_thought: (Left wrist. Always. Bapak gave it to me at the airport and said something about time and I was too busy trying not to cry to hear it.)
interactables.flag_condition_note: If dream00 was completed, append: (Somebody was wearing one of these. In the dream. Left wrist.)

interactables.label: The mirror on the back of the door
interactables.internal_thought: (Transition glasses still dark from yesterday's walk. I look like someone who's about to be asked if he's okay.)
interactables.follow_up: (I don't look for long. I never do.)

interactables.label: Taxi Driver poster, corner peeling
interactables.internal_thought: (Mason thinks I put it up to look interesting. I put it up because a man alone in a room talking to himself is the most honest thing I've seen on film.)
interactables.follow_up: (Fight Club's underneath it. I ran out of wall.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: Fiz. I can hear your alarm through the wall. It's been going for eleven minutes.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (Eleven minutes.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: I'm not gonna write you up. I'm just gonna stand out here judging you until you turn it off.

choices.choice_text: "You've been up since five, haven't you."

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: Since four-forty. Somebody set off the fire panel in C-wing and guess whose problem that is.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: Hall check in ten. And Fiz — eat something today. Something with a shape. Not the vending machine.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (Somewhere between the door and the stairs my brain runs the thing again. A hallway. Someone raising a gun. Me, calm.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (Always calm, in the version where it happens. Nobody's ever raised anything at me. My head just likes rehearsing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Hall check. Twenty-two doors, one clipboard, one RA who's been awake since before the sun.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sandra Johnson
dialogue_sequence.text: Hey — hey, Fiz. Quick thing. Did Zoey say anything to you? About the weekend?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Sandra asks me about Zoey roughly twice a week. Zoey has never once said anything to me about the weekend.)

choices.choice_text: "No. She doesn't talk to me, Sandra."
"Why are you asking me and not her?"

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sandra Johnson
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Right. No. Yeah. Obviously.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She orbits Zoey the way a moon orbits something with actual mass. I don't think she knows there's a difference between being included and being tolerated.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elena Ward
dialogue_sequence.text: Gina. Panel log, C-wing. And I need it before Carter asks, not after.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
dialogue_sequence.text: It's on your desk. It's been on your desk since five.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elena Ward
dialogue_sequence.text: ...It has. Sorry. Long night.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Ms. Ward went to school here. She doesn't advertise it. Somebody told me once and she's never brought it up, which is its own kind of answer.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elena Ward
dialogue_sequence.text: It's November. It's always a long night in November.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elena Ward
dialogue_sequence.text: Get to breakfast, Hafizh.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Nobody here uses my actual name. She does. Every time. Gets it right, too.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: There he is. My most reliable customer and my worst tipper.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: Sit. Booth by the window's still got heat in it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: She always remembers what I order.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: Honey, you've ordered the same thing since October last year. That's not memory, that's arithmetic.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She remembers the no-bacon without me ever having to explain it. Twice she's caught the kitchen and sent a plate back herself.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's not arithmetic. Even when the rest of the town tries to forget everything, she remembers the small stuff.)

exploration.prompt: Seventeen minutes before you need to leave.

interactables.label: Half-burned photograph behind the counter
interactables.internal_thought: (Group shot. Diner staff, sometime before. The right third is gone — burned, not torn. Whoever's missing from it was standing on that side.)
interactables.follow_up: (Linda notices me looking. Linda always notices me looking.)

interactables.label: The jukebox
interactables.internal_thought: (Unplugged. Has been the whole year. There's dust in the coin slot deep enough to have a texture.)

interactables.label: Small brass plaque by the door
interactables.internal_thought: (IN MEMORY OF THOSE WHO STAYED. No names. Just that.)
interactables.follow_up: (A memorial that can't bring itself to list anybody. That's the most Arcadia Bay object in Arcadia Bay.)

interactables.label: Something on the pole across the street
interactables.internal_thought: (New camera. Grey housing, clean bracket. It wasn't there in September — I've shot that corner a dozen times and I'd know.)
interactables.follow_up: (It's pointed at the diner door. Not the road. The door.)

interactables.label: The laminated menu
interactables.internal_thought: (TWO WHALES DINER is still showing under the new print where the lamination's lifted. She reprinted over it instead of starting fresh.)

interactables.label: The man in the corner booth
interactables.internal_thought: (Brandon Montgomery. Same booth, same time, every morning I've been here. I've never seen him eat.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
post_exploration_sequence.text: You know this place used to be packed at seven? Line out the door. Fishermen, truckers, half the school skipping first period.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
post_exploration_sequence.text: Now it's you, Brandon back there, and whoever's lost on the coast road.

choices.choice_text: "It still says Two Whales under the print."

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
post_exploration_sequence.text: Oh, honey. Everything changed. That's the whole answer and nobody in this town will give you a longer one.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
post_exploration_sequence.text: I kept the name underneath because I couldn't afford new menus. That's the boring truth and I'd appreciate you letting it stay boring.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
post_exploration_sequence.text: Eat your eggs.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Brandon Montgomery
post_exploration_sequence.text: You keep looking at that picture.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (He hasn't moved in twenty minutes. I didn't think he was awake.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Brandon Montgomery
post_exploration_sequence.text: Everyone does, first year. Then they stop. You'll stop.

choices.choice_text: [Say nothing. Go back to your coffee.]

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Brandon Montgomery
post_exploration_sequence.text: Because it's easier. And because after a while you notice the people who didn't stop looking aren't around anymore.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Brandon Montgomery
post_exploration_sequence.text: That's not a threat, kid. That's just the attendance record.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (He puts a five on the table for a coffee he didn't drink and goes out into the rain without a coat.)

scenes.location: Arcadia Bay — Coast Road, then Blackwell front lawn

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Twenty minutes on foot. I could take the bus. I've never taken the bus.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Rain that can't commit. Trees down to bare wire. The whole town the colour of an unwashed window.)

exploration.prompt: The long way. It's always the long way.

interactables.label: New builds along the seafront
interactables.internal_thought: (Everything here is either ten years old or a hundred. Nothing in between. The town has a decade-shaped hole in its architecture.)
interactables.follow_up: (Same contractor plate on every hoarding. CROSS INDUSTRIES — REBUILDING ARCADIA BAY.)

interactables.label: Another camera, junction of Cedar and Front
interactables.internal_thought: (That's two this morning. Same grey housing. Same clean bracket. Nobody in this town has money for two-week-old brackets.)

interactables.label: Weathered notice on the bus shelter
interactables.internal_thought: (Sun-bleached to nothing. You can make out the word HAVE and half a phone number. Whoever it was, they've been gone longer than the paper's lasted.)

interactables.label: The bay itself
interactables.internal_thought: (Flat grey water. Somewhere under it is a whole version of this place that nobody will describe to me.)
interactables.follow_up: (I love water. I've loved being under it since I was six. That's the part I can't square — how something I find that peaceful took this much from everyone here.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (Kieran's at the shelter. He's always at the shelter. He doesn't take the bus either.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: Morning.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
post_exploration_sequence.text: Morning.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (We walk the last eight minutes together and say nothing else and it's the least exhausting eight minutes of the day.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
post_exploration_sequence.text: Four of them. Front, Cedar, the lot behind the church, one on the cliff road.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
post_exploration_sequence.text: Went up over three nights in September. Nobody asked. Nobody's said a word about it since.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: You counted them.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
post_exploration_sequence.text: I count everything. It's not a talent, it's a condition.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (That's more words than Kieran has said to me in a week, and every one of them was load-bearing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (You hear Amber before you see her. That's the entire point of Amber.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: OH MY GOD — everyone. Everyone. Look who wore the same jacket four days running!

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: Riley. Riley, look at me. Look at the light, babe, I need your eyes in it, the ring's on.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Amber. Get the fucking phone out of my face.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Lila West
dialogue_sequence.text: Ooh. She talks. Write it down, someone write it down.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: Enough, Lila. She's already embarrassing herself. You don't need to hold her hand through it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's the trick. Zoey never throws the punch. She just stands close enough to be in the photo.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jake Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Hey. Exchange student. You dropped something.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: He didn't drop anything, man.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jake Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: He dropped his fucking passport, Luke. That was the joke. God.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The hallway does the thing where it gets quiet and everybody keeps walking. Nobody looks. That's this town in one hallway.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (My hands are shaking. Not from fear. From having nowhere to put it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (And under that, quieter, in a voice I don't recognise yet: they only do this because it works.)

choices.choice_text: "That was a shit joke, Jake. Even Luke didn't get it."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jake Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Say that again.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: Jake. Bell.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She calls him off like a dog and he goes, and the worst part is he doesn't notice she did it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: Okay that's going up. That's going UP, that's a clip, that is content.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Luke doesn't move for a second. He looks at Riley, then at the floor, then he goes after Jake.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (File that. I don't know why yet.)

scenes.location: Blackwell Academy — Second floor, disabled bathroom

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's on the floor with her back against the pipe. The one bathroom in this building with a lock that works.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't say anything nice. I'll cry and then I'll be angry that I cried.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Okay.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I sit down on the tile. Not next to her. Across. Enough space that she gets to choose.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: ...You're doing the thing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: The sitting-down-and-shutting-up thing. Who taught you that?

choices.choice_text: "Nobody. I just didn't have anything worth saying."
"My mother. She never fixed anything either. She just stayed."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: That's the most you've ever told me about her.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: A year, Fiz. That's the most in a year.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's not angry. She's counting. She's been counting.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: It's not even about Amber. Amber's a wasp. You don't take a wasp personally.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: It's that forty people watched and the bell rang and everyone just went to class.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: This whole town does that. Something happens, everyone sees it, and then the bell rings.

choices.choice_text: "You're not talking about the hallway anymore."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: ...No. I'm not.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Forget it. I'm being dramatic on a bathroom floor, it's a whole genre.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's twisting the bracelet. Silver, thin, too big for her. She does that when she's deciding whether to say a true thing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She decides not to. She almost always decides not to.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Cliffs after last period? I'll bring the sketchbook, you bring the camera, we can be pretentious together.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Deal.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Owen Rhys
dialogue_sequence.text: Assignment. Due Friday. One image. Here's the brief, and I want you to sit with it before you groan at me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Owen Rhys
dialogue_sequence.text: Photograph something this town would rather you didn't look at.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ezra Lang
dialogue_sequence.text: That's not a brief, that's a mood board.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Owen Rhys
dialogue_sequence.text: It's a brief. You just don't like the ones you can't win on technique.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Rhys has been here two years. He talks about photography like it's a way of behaving rather than a subject.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He also has a folder on his desk labelled 2013 — DO NOT TEACH, in his own handwriting, and I've never asked.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: I've been shooting near the old lighthouse. There's a light down there that doesn't behave.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: I mean — the fog does something to it. Obviously. I'm not being weird.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She took it back before anyone made her. She does that a lot. I've started noticing how many people here do that.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ezra Lang
dialogue_sequence.text: Fiz shoots the lighthouse constantly. Might want to pick something else, Sienna. He gets precious about his spots.

choices.choice_text: "Shoot it. I'd like to see your version."
[Let Ezra have it. Look at the brief.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: It's — okay, don't laugh. Long exposure, thirty seconds, tripod, nothing touching it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: And in the frame the light sweeps twice. Left, then right. The lighthouse hasn't worked since 2013. There's nothing down there to sweep.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ezra Lang
dialogue_sequence.text: Or your tripod moved.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: Or my tripod moved. Yeah. Probably that.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Left, then right.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: You'll get marked down, you know. For doing the brief honestly.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: Not by him. By whoever reads it after him. Nobody here grades honesty well.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Olivia. Two seats over all semester. This is the fourth thing she's ever said to me and all four have been correct.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: Because I grew up here and I'd rather be marked down than pretend.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She turns the notebook so I can see. Not offering it — just not hiding it, which from her is the same gesture.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Pencil. Two girls at the lighthouse, holding hands. One has a camera. The other one's hair is shaded in darker — filled in, deliberate.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: I drew that before I knew who they were.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: I know how that sounds. I'm not asking you to believe it. I'm telling you because you asked and I don't do the thing where I make it smaller.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Olivia Calder
dialogue_sequence.text: You should come out to the cliffs sometime. It's not a line. I just think you'd like the quiet.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: Heard about the hallway. Heard Jake tried a passport joke and ate shit on it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Mason.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: What? I'm proud of him. Our boy's developing a mouth.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: And Jake's developing a grudge. Those aren't the same thing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: It was one sentence.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: It's never one sentence with him. His dad owns the company rebuilding the town, Fiz. He's never been told no by anyone whose name isn't Cross.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: Guys — guys, hold on, I'm live. SAY HI TO THE GRID.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: This is Fiz. He edits my thumbnails, he's better at it than me, and he has never once said hello to chat. Fiz. FIZ. Four hundred people.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: THAT'S THE CLIP. That's the whole stream, I can go home.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Kieran pushes his fries into the middle of the table. He does this every day. We have never discussed it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
dialogue_sequence.text: Wrote something on my board this morning. "The town rebuilt everything except the part that remembers."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't know if it's good. Don't really care.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: That's depressing as hell, man.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: It's not wrong, though.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Pete's brother. Ten years this month. Nobody says it, and Pete keeps eating like the sentence didn't come out of him.)

choices.choice_text: [Change the subject. Give him the exit.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Yeah. It's just the month.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Mom does this thing where she cooks for five. Still. Every November.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Anyway. Mason, tell him about the car.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: OH. The car. Okay so it makes a noise now —

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Mason talks for six minutes about a noise. He's not stupid. He's just the only one of us who knows how to fill a hole in the conversation.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (This is the good part of the day. I want to remember that later, when I'm deciding things.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Free period. The library's the only room in this building where nobody performs.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: You're the exchange student. Hafizh.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: Sorry. That came out like an accusation. I'm Alice. I work the desk Tuesdays.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Carter. Same as the principal. Same eyes, and she carries herself like she's apologising for the surname.)

interactables.label: Yearbook shelf
interactables.follow_up: (Not a gap on the shelf. The shelf's been re-spaced so there isn't one. Somebody moved the books along.)

interactables.label: Local history section
interactables.internal_thought: (Arcadia Bay: A Coastal History. Published 2019. The chapter on the storm is four pages and reads like an insurance form.)
interactables.follow_up: (Casualty figure given as "significant." That's the number. That's the whole number.)

interactables.label: Door marked ARCHIVE — STAFF ONLY
interactables.internal_thought: (Newer lock than the door it's in. Card reader. In a school library.)

interactables.label: Gazette microfiche reader
interactables.internal_thought: (October 2013 spool is here. It's blank for nine days. Not missing — blank. Somebody fed film through a reader and it came out clean.)

interactables.label: The corner table with the paper on it
interactables.internal_thought: (Taki Kimura. Six documents, four highlighters, one very committed expression.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
post_exploration_sequence.text: You've been at that shelf for four minutes. Which means you counted.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
post_exploration_sequence.text: Everyone else walks past it. You counted.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
post_exploration_sequence.text: Not in the county system. Not in the state archive. Not on any resale site, and believe me.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
